title: Intelligent and Automatic System Interface Control System for Users with Disabilities
summary: An Ethiopian project combines vision models and eye tracking for computer control. Functional benefits for users remain intended while development continues.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: An Ethiopian project combines vision models and eye tracking for computer control. Functional benefits for users remain intended while development continues. Interface-control project under development.
purpose: Enable people with hand impairments to operate digital devices.
developer: Addis Ababa Science and Technology University

ratings.reason: People with hand or mobility impairments are intended to control computers hands-free.

ai_role.statement: The chapter describes this system as supporting the stated purpose. Its causal contribution to the benefit has not been separately assessed.

evidence.citation: Contributed use case in International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact, 2025. Information current as of June 2025. The reported outcomes are attributed to the submitting project, not an independent outcome evaluation by ITU.
evidence.title: Use Case 9: Intelligent and Automatic System Interface Control System for Users with Disabilities

produced_by: Causal conditions are not established separately in the extracted chapter.
must_hold: Mappings from recognized gestures to interface actions

headline: Eye gestures for hands-free computer control

revisions.change: Added the sourced case with separate benefit depth, beneficiary, evidence confidence, and outcome status assessments.

claim_basis: The makers' report is on file. There is no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
